feedback.problem: Which of the following is the graph of  $y=-{(\frac{1}{3})}^{x}-6?$
feedback.worked_solution:
To plot the given function, we follow these steps:

- We take the curve $y={(\frac{1}{3})}^{x}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13932041/assets/7b9f7e5ca81a615cb16ccb7a69f9d1669366944d0615041ed8e960f59b8e24dd.png)

- Reflect it in the $x$-axis to give $y=-{(\frac{1}{3})}^{x}.$ The $y$-intercept moves from $(0,1)$ to $(0,-1)$ but the horizontal asymptote stays at $y=0.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13932041/assets/00e5e14399b9fd259327e1c8fbbccd43018df8a4c78b7ed7d957819c81eef7f2.png)

- Then, vertically shift it by $6$ units down to give $y=-{(\frac{1}{3})}^{x}-6.$ The point $(0,-1)$ moves to $(-1,-7)$ and the horizontal asymptote moves from from $y=0$ to $y=-6.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13932041/assets/c99dc12a5a34672fa5b5bd180d777c1640b657d0725d115b9f6decfab6296b18.png)
